_README: The generation catalog. One entry per way of making something on Blotato.
Any skill calls these by id through scripts/blotato/generate.py; nothing else should
hardcode a template id. Edit this file to add a technique - no Python change needed.
cost_credits: measured from the live balance, never guessed. null = not measured yet.
reliability:  proven | partial | unproven | failed  (with a one-line note saying why)
route:        api (works anywhere with the key) | web (needs OpenCLI + a logged-in Chrome)

techniques.name: Words to a picture
techniques.returns: image (rendered as a one-slide video; needs a frame grab)
techniques.notes: Output arrives as video; a .png needs frame one pulled with ffmpeg.

techniques.name: A picture plus words to a new picture
techniques.cost_source: measured 2026-09-19, twice, from the live balance
techniques.notes: Excellent stylist, unreliable copier. It REDRAWS the reference: on Drew's logo it turned a wide flat dome into a tall horseshoe, twice, even when the prompt demanded the outline be kept. Fine for backgrounds and mood frames. Never for a logo, a badge, a watermark, or a character that must persist - use route web for those. Returns a JPEG whatever you name the file, and always 4:5.

techniques.name: Put my own file on Blotato
techniques.notes: Worked first try on a 1024x1024 PNG. Use this before any technique that takes a ref.

techniques.name: Scenes to a finished video (pictures, motion, voice, captions)
techniques.cost_source: measured 2026-09-19: 0 with uploaded media, 70 per GENERATED+animated scene
techniques.notes: The backbone, and the thing to build on. Each scene's mediaSource is EITHER an uploaded image/video OR a text prompt, so one call covers picture-to-clip, words-to-clip, voice and captions. 1-20 scenes. animateAiImages only affects AI-generated images - an uploaded still gets the free zoom instead. trimToVoiceover fits the cut to the narration. Known flaw: generated stills come back wide and are letterboxed into a 9:16 frame.
techniques.voice_note: Use the FULL string, e.g. 'Brian (American, deep)'. A bare 'Brian' is rejected with http 422 (free, caught before any spend).
techniques.cost_note: Two very different prices in one template. A scene whose mediaSource is an UPLOADED picture costs 0 - voice, captions and the Ken Burns zoom all come free, and the picture is reproduced exactly. A scene generated from a text prompt and animated costs about 70. So: pay for stills once, assemble free.

techniques.name: Talking video with the same character throughout
techniques.cost_source: measured 2026-09-19: 800 for a 2-scene video = 400 per scene
techniques.notes: AVOID. It does hold one character across scenes - same face, clothes and props indoors and outdoors - but it IGNORED the character described (asked for a weathered detective in his fifties in a brown overcoat, got a man in his twenties in fantasy gear) and wrote gibberish text into the frame. At 400 a scene it is 5.7x video.story for a worse match. The cheap, exact answer to the same-face problem is video.story with the character still UPLOADED.

techniques.name: Join clips, trim, caption, add music
techniques.notes: Not generation. Free fallback if it ever charges: the local ffmpeg assembler in ../cinco-vid.

techniques.name: Style reference + likeness reference to a new picture
techniques.cost_source: measured 2026-09-19 on the website: nano-banana-2/edit, 30 from the live balance
techniques.notes: PROVEN. Editor > Image > Generate > pick an Edit model > Reference Images > Pick images (up to 14, from the video's scene images or an upload). Style from the alley frame + Drew's logo as likeness -> wooden sign in the alley with the logo EXACT. A single-ref neon test redrew the logo as a double tube, so name the likeness image explicitly in the prompt and say 'exact shape, proportions and color unchanged'. Click path and OpenCLI traps: docs/web-abilities.md.

techniques.name: A clip from a specific named model (Kling, Veo, Runway...)
techniques.cost_source: measured 2026-09-19: framepack 55 (image-to-video); site prices for the rest listed in models
techniques.notes: PROVEN with Framepack: Editor > click a generated image > Create Animated Image > Animate tab > model + motion prompt. 5 s at 480x848 (soft). Kling adds End Image = morph. Output is videogen2-anim-*.mp4 on the timeline.

techniques.name: Words to a clip with voice baked in (Veo 3.1 Fast on the website)
techniques.cost_source: measured 2026-09-19: veo3.1/fast 4 s with audio = 200; site shows 50/sec with audio, 35/sec without; veo3 flat 1250; mochi-v1 135
techniques.notes: PROVEN. Editor > Video > Generate. One-paragraph prompt with the spoken line in quotes -> hand-drawn detective in a gaslit alley, mouth moving, real audio track, 720x1280, 4.0 s. This is the tutorial's baked-voice method. Dear per scene (200 per 4 s) versus video.story at ~70, so hero scenes only unless lip-sync matters. Output is videogen2-vid-*.mp4 on the timeline.
